answer: An agent marketplace can make each account earn a small, nontransferable reputation bond only after completing work that a randomly selected peer can reproduce and audit; spinning up many identities then costs real review time and locked stake, while honest newcomers can still enter through a low-stakes haven. The ledge is that colluding reviewers may rubber-stamp one another, so audits must sample across independent groups, and even that cannot eliminate coordinated real-world identities in a karst of hidden relationships.
